When CRM makes sense

CRM helps when it is hard to determine who is handling an enquiry, when the next contact should happen, and what was promised to the client. A simple contact list alone will not solve this problem. What is needed are stages, clear ownership, and a link to subsequent fulfilment.

We design the system around the actual work of sales reps and managers. First, we check whether the current tool can be adapted. We propose a new system only where the existing solution does not support a crucial part of the process.

What implementation can include

  • Collecting enquiries from forms and agreed channels.
  • Sales stages, enquiry owner and the next step.
  • Quotes and pricing with established rules.
  • Handing over an accepted order for fulfilment.
  • Roles, change history, and reports needed by the team.
  • Data migration and ERP integration, if included in the scope.

Example: manufacturer process

Dopina for manufacturers connects sales work with pricing and fulfilment of pavilions. We develop the solution based on the STAGO implementation experience. This is an example of a project where CRM is part of the company's operational process.

See Dopina for manufacturers.

Price and scope limits

Pricing is influenced by roles, number of workflows, migration, pricing rules, and integrations.

Before starting, we define acceptance criteria, external costs, maintenance, and data handover procedures. If uncertainty prevents pricing, we propose a separate analysis.

What to prepare for the call

Sample sales stages, a list of current tools, and two or three examples where time or information is currently lost are enough. Do not send customer data at the beginning — the process can be discussed using an example.

CRM or ERP? Check the difference before deciding.
